whirlpool noun

also eddy, vortex, maelstrom

classical

Liv. 23.19.11
Quint. 8.2.7: vertex est contorta in sē aqua

vertex, verticis m.

noun, third declension

whirlpool, eddy

Water turning in on itself; also the crown of the head and a mountain top. The old spelling vortex was out of use by Cicero’s day (Lewis & Short, after Quint. 1.7.25).

Other words

  • gurges, gurgitis m. — a deep, swirling water; whirlpool

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 21.5.14; Andresian p. 23

    The deep, raging water itself, against the shallows (Livy: per mediōs gurgitēs, opposed to vada); in poetry any stretch of water.

Examples

  • rapidus vorat aequore vertex

    a swift whirlpool swallows it in the seaVerg. A. 1.117

See also river, sea, wave.

SourcesLewis & Short: vertex · Lewis & Short: gurges

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 23.
